**DECLARATION OF AUTHORSHIP**

**ABSTRACT**

Second-hand trading often requires users to switch between platforms to discover products, contact sellers, negotiate prices, and track transactions. This capstone project presents **ReStore**, a consumer-to-consumer mobile marketplace designed to bring these activities into one application. Users can post and manage listings, search and filter products, save favorites, communicate in real time, negotiate prices, propose exchanges, and receive notifications. Sellers can also purchase listing boosts through VNPay, while administrators can moderate listings, handle reports, manage users, and monitor platform activity.

The mobile application is designed with Flutter. A Node.js and Express.js backend implements business logic and APIs, with Prisma and PostgreSQL managing persistent data. Socket.IO supports real-time messaging, Cloudinary stores uploaded images, and Firebase Cloud Messaging delivers push notifications. An AI assistant helps users find relevant listings and understand marketplace features through backend-controlled access to listing information.

The project covers requirements analysis, system design, implementation, and testing of the main marketplace workflows. ReStore aims to make second-hand buying, selling, and exchanging more convenient while providing tools to support trust and platform management.

# **CHAPTER 1: INTRODUCTION** {#chapter-1:-introduction}

## **1.1 Problem Statement** {#1.1-problem-statement}

The rapid growth of online marketplaces has increased the demand for convenient platforms for buying, selling, and exchanging second-hand listings. However, users may face difficulties in finding suitable listings, communicating with buyers or sellers, negotiating prices, and managing their transactions. The problem is to build a user-friendly mobile application which connects buyers and sellers in one platform. The system should provide users the ability to post listings, search and filter, set favorites, message, offers, transaction history and real time notifications to provide users the convenience and efficiency of second hand trading.

## **1.2 Purpose and Requirements** {#1.2-purpose-and-requirements}

The purpose of the Restore Second-Hand Marketplace Mobile Application is to develop a modern, convenient, and user-friendly platform that connects buyers and sellers of second-hand listings. The application supports the complete second-hand trading process, from listing discovery and communication to price negotiation and transaction management. The system aims to:

* Provide a convenient marketplace browsing and shopping experience with listing search, filtering, and detailed views.  
* Allow users to create accounts, log in securely, and manage their personal profiles.  
* Enable sellers to create, update, and manage listing listings with descriptions, prices, categories, conditions, and images.  
* Help buyers find suitable listings through keyword search, category selection, sorting, and filtering.  
* Allow users to save listings to a favorites list for later viewing.  
* Support direct messaging between buyers and sellers.  
* Maintain purchase and sales histories so users can track their transactions.  
* Deliver real-time notifications for messages, offers, listing updates, and transaction events.  
* Provide administrators with tools to manage users, listings, reports, categories, and platform activities.  
* Build a maintainable and responsive mobile application using Flutter, PostgreSQL, and Node.js/Express.

## **1.3 Scope and Target Users** {#1.3-scope-and-target-users}

The system focuses on developing the core functions of a mobile marketplace for second-hand listings. It provides a shared platform where users can act as buyers, sellers, or both. The application is designed to make second-hand trading more accessible, organized, and efficient.  
The main target users include:

* Buyers looking for affordable second-hand listings.  
* Sellers who want to list and sell listings they no longer use.  
* Users interested in exchanging listings with other members of the platform.  
* Administrators responsible for managing users, listing listings, categories, reports, and inappropriate content.

Expected functional scope includes:

* User registration, login, logout, and authentication.  
* User profile creation and management.  
* Listing listing creation, editing, deletion, and status management.  
* Uploading and displaying listing images.  
* Listing browsing, searching, sorting, and filtering.  
* Listing detail pages containing seller and listing information.  
* Favorite-listing management.  
* Real-time buyer–seller messaging.  
* Price-offer submission and negotiation.  
* Listing exchange requests and management.  
* Purchase and sales transaction history.  
* Real-time notifications for messages, offers, exchanges, and transaction updates.  
* Listing and user reporting.  
* Administrator management of users, listings, categories, reports, and platform content.

# **Chapter 2: Background Knowledge** {#chapter-2:-background-knowledge}

## **2.1 Development Tools and Environment** {#2.1-development-tools-and-environment}

The Restore Second-Hand Marketplace Mobile Application will be developed using Flutter, Node.js, Express.js, PostgreSQL, Prisma, and Cloudinary. Socket.IO will support real-time communication, while Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) will provide push notifications. This technology stack separates the mobile interface, backend business logic, database access, and media storage to support system maintenance and future expansion. 

* **Flutter** is used to develop the mobile user interface. Its widget-based architecture supports reusable components and provides a consistent user experience on Android and iOS devices.  
* **Express.js**, running on Node.js, functions as the backend web framework. Express simplifies the creation of robust RESTful APIs, handling HTTP requests and server-side logic efficiently.  
* **Dart** is the primary programming language used for frontend development. It supports object-oriented programming, asynchronous operations, and strong type checking.  
* **Node.js** provides the backend runtime environment. Its asynchronous architecture supports concurrent requests and operations such as listing management, offer processing, and transaction updates.  
* **PostgreSQL** will serve as the primary relational database. It will store structured data such as users, listing listings, categories, favorites, offers, conversations, messages, and notification records.  
* **Prisma ORM** will provide the database access layer between the Node.js backend and PostgreSQL. It will support schema definition, database migrations, and type-safe database queries.  
* **Cloudinary** will handle media storage and delivery for listing images, user avatars, and chat attachments. PostgreSQL will store the associated media URLs and identifiers.

To enhance development listingivity and maintainability, additional tools and libraries are integrated:

* **Flutter’s development tools** provide hot reload, debugging, and application builds, helping developers implement and test mobile interfaces efficiently   
* **Flutter Material widgets** will provide interface components such as buttons, forms, navigation elements, dialogs, and cards.  
*  **Authentication and authorization libraries** will support JWT-based access tokens, refresh-token handling, and secure password hashing. The backend will validate user identity and permissions for both REST API requests and Socket.IO events.  
* **Socket.IO** will support real-time messaging, typing indicators, read receipts, and online/offline status updates. Messages will be stored in PostgreSQL, and application-level synchronization will retrieve missed messages after reconnection. Presence tracking will account for connection timeouts and multiple active devices.  
* **Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM)** will deliver push notifications for new messages and relevant marketplace events. The Flutter application will receive notifications through Firebase Messaging, while the Node.js backend will send them through the Firebase Admin SDK. Device registration tokens will be associated with user accounts. Firebase will be used for push notifications; PostgreSQL will remain the primary application database.  
* **OpenAPI and Swagger UI** will document REST API endpoints, request formats, authentication requirements, and response structures. Documentation will cover the implemented marketplace modules, including authentication, users, listings, offers, conversations, and notifications.  
* **Git** will provide version control for tracking source-code changes and supporting collaboration.  
* **An email delivery service** support account verification and password-reset emails

## **2.2 Programming Languages and Frameworks** {#2.2-programming-languages-and-frameworks}

Dart forms the foundation of the mobile application, while JavaScript is used for backend development. The mobile frontend communicates with backend services through RESTful APIs and real-time events, keeping interface development and business logic independently maintainable.  
The frontend uses Flutter widgets, navigation, state management, and reusable components. The client code is organized into feature modules for authentication, profiles, listing listings, search, favorites, messaging, offers, notifications, and AI chatbot assistance.  
On the backend, Express.js runs on Node.js to handle API requests and business logic. Server modules use Prisma to access PostgreSQL, while shared middleware handles authentication, authorization, validation, rate limiting, and errors. Cloudinary manages images, Socket.IO supports real-time chat and presence updates, and Firebase Cloud Messaging delivers push notifications. The backend also integrates an external LLM API to provide chatbot assistance using relevant listing information.

## **2.3 Applied Methods and Technical Approaches** {#2.3-applied-methods-and-technical-approaches}

Several best practices and technical methods are employed to ensure the system’s functionality, security, and performance:

* **Authentication and Authorization:** Users will receive signed JWT access tokens after login. The backend will validate tokens and permissions before allowing access to protected APIs and chat events.  
* **Session and Security Management:** Token expiration, refresh mechanisms, and secure mobile storage will protect authentication sessions. HTTPS, input validation, password hashing, and rate limiting will help safeguard user data.  
* **Listing and Offer Management:** Users will create listings, save favorites, and submit purchase or exchange offers. The backend will verify listing ownership and offer status changes, while PostgreSQL will maintain transaction records.  
* **Real-Time Messaging and Notifications:** Socket.IO will support messaging, online/offline status, and read receipts. Messages will be stored in PostgreSQL and synchronized after reconnection. Firebase Cloud Messaging will deliver push notifications for messages and marketplace updates.  
* **AI Chatbot Integration:** The backend will connect to an external LLM API and retrieve relevant listing information through Prisma. Controlled tool calling will support listing searches and availability checks while enforcing user permissions.  
* **Role-Based Access Control:** Administrators will manage users, listings, categories, and reports. Backend permission checks will restrict administrative functions and protect user-owned resources.  
* **Deployment Architecture:** The Node.js/Express backend will be deployed on Amazon EC2 to support RESTful APIs and persistent Socket.IO connections. PostgreSQL will be hosted on Amazon RDS, while Cloudinary will handle media storage and delivery. Flutter builds will be distributed for mobile installation and testing. 

## **2.4 Listing Background and Market Context** {#2.4-listing-background-and-market-context}

Consumer-to-consumer (C2C) marketplaces connect individuals who want to buy, sell, or exchange listings. Restore follows this model by providing a mobile platform for both new and second-hand goods, where each registered user can act as a buyer and a seller.  
The application supports listing listings, search and filtering, favorites, direct messaging, and price negotiation. Users can offer listings for sale, exchange, or both, while transaction history and notifications help them track their activities.  
A chatbot provides guidance on application features, transaction procedures, and platform rules. Users can also report inappropriate listings or behavior for administrator review.  
At the administrative level, the platform supports user management, listing moderation, category management, and report handling to maintain an organized marketplace.

# **Chapter 3: Analysis & Solution Design** {#chapter-3:-analysis-&-solution-design}

## **3.1 System Architecture Overview** {#3.1-system-architecture-overview}

**Frontend (Flutter \+ Clean Architecture \+ Feature-Based Architecture)** 

* **Pages and modules:** Authentication, Home, Listing Discovery, Listing Detail, Create/Edit Listing, Favorites, Profile, Address Management, Chat, Offers, Exchanges, Transaction History, Reports, Notifications, AI Chatbot, and Admin Management.  
* **Code organization:** Each feature is divided into Presentation, Domain, and Data layers. Shared components support reusable widgets, API communication, and error handling.  
* **State management:** Application state is managed separately for each feature, including authentication, listings, messaging, offers, exchanges, and notifications.  
* **Authentication:** The application supports email/password authentication and Google Sign-In through backend services. JWT access tokens authenticate protected requests, while refresh tokens support session renewal. Tokens are stored using secure mobile storage.

**Backend (Node.js \+ Express.js \+ Prisma)**

* **Services:** Authentication, User, Listing, Category, Favorite, Chat, Offer, Exchange, Transaction, Report, Notification, Admin, Statistics, Media, and AI Chatbot.  
* **Middleware:** JWT verification, role-based authorization, request validation, rate limiting, error handling, and file upload handling.  
* **Database access:** Prisma manages PostgreSQL queries, relationships, migrations, and database transactions.  
* **Real-time communication:** Socket.IO supports buyer-seller messaging, typing indicators, read receipts, presence updates, and offer or exchange status updates. Missed messages are retrieved from the database after reconnection.

**Database (PostgreSQL)**

* **Tables:** users, addresses, listings, categories, favorites, conversations, conversation\_members, messages, offers, exchanges, transactions, reports, notifications, device\_tokens, refresh\_tokens, and email\_verifications.  
* **Data integrity:** Foreign keys, constraints, and database transactions maintain relationships and consistent updates. PostgreSQL stores persistent application data, including message and transaction history.

**External Integrations**

* **Media:** Cloudinary stores listing images, user avatars, and chat attachments.  
* **Email:** Nodemailer connects to an email service to send registration verification and password-reset OTPs.  
* **Google Sign-In:** Google identity verification supports account registration and login through the backend.  
* **Push notifications:** Firebase Cloud Messaging delivers notifications to mobile devices. Firebase is used only for push notifications.  
* **AI chatbot:** An external LLM API provides application guidance and marketplace assistance through backend-controlled access to relevant information.

**Deployment** (AWS)

* **Backend:** Amazon EC2 hosts the Node.js/Express application and Socket.IO connections.  
* **Database:** Amazon RDS hosts PostgreSQL.  
* **Mobile application:** Flutter builds are distributed for installation and testing, with HTTPS securing communication with the backend.

### **3.1.1 Three-layer Architecture** {#3.1.1-three-layer-architecture}

![A diagram of a software processAI-generated content may be incorrect.][image2]

###### *Figure 3.1.1: The Three-Layer Architecture* {#figure-3.1.1:-the-three-layer-architecture}

The Three-Layer Architecture divides an application into three logical layers:  
**Presentation Layer (GUI / User Interface)**: This layer is responsible for all interaction with the end user. It includes the visual components of the system, such as screens, forms, and input fields. Its main responsibilities are:

* Receiving user input.  
* Displaying listings, messages, offers, and notifications.   
* Performing basic validation, such as checking required fields and input formats, before sending requests to the backend. ).

The Presentation Layer focuses on the user interface and communicates with backend services through RESTful APIs and Socket.IO.   
**Business Logic Layer (BLL)**: Contains the core business rules. It processes requests from the Presentation Layer, validates data, applies business logic, and coordinates data flow to and from the Data Access Layer.  
**Data Access Layer (DAL)**: Responsible for all communication with the database. It performs CRUD operations (Create, Read, Update, Delete) and hides database details from the upper layers.  
Overall, this three-layer approach increases modularity, testability, and scalability. Each layer focuses on a single set of responsibilities, which makes the system easier to develop, debug, and extend over time.

### **3.1.2 Clean Architecture in Flutter**  {#3.1.2-clean-architecture-in-flutter}

Clean Architecture separates each Flutter feature into:

* **Presentation:** Displays data, collects user input, and manages interface state.   
* **Domain:** Defines entities, use cases, and repository interfaces independently of UI and external services.   
* **Data:** Implements repository interfaces and handles communication with backend APIs and local storage. 

![A diagram of a processAI-generated content may be incorrect.][image3]

###### *Figure 3.1.2: Clean Architecture Layers in Flutter* {#figure-3.1.2:-clean-architecture-layers-in-flutter}

### **3.1.3 Feature-Based Source Code Organization**  {#3.1.3-feature-based-source-code-organization}

The implemented source code will be organized into feature modules on both the frontend and backend. These modules cover account management, listing discovery, listings, messaging, offers, exchanges, and administration. Each Flutter feature follows Presentation, Domain, and Data layers, while backend features contain routes, controllers, and services. Common functionality, including authentication, database access, media handling, and notifications, will be shared across modules to reduce duplication and improve maintainability. 

##### *Table 3.1.3: Domain Separation in Source Code* {#table-3.1.3:-domain-separation-in-source-code}

| Layer | Marketplace Features  | Communication and Support  | Shared Infrastructure |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Frontend** | Flutter modules for profiles, listings, search, favorites, offers, exchanges, transaction history, and administration.  | Chat, notifications, reports, and AI chatbot screens with their state management and data-access components.  | Reusable widgets, navigation, API client, secure token storage, Socket.IO client, and error handling. . |
| **Backend** | Express routes, controllers, and services for users, listings, categories, favorites, offers, exchanges, transactions, and administration.  | Services for conversations, messages, notifications, reports, and AI chatbot assistance. . | JWT verification, authorization, request validation, Prisma, Socket.IO, Cloudinary, email delivery, FCM, and error handling. . |

## **3.2 Core Algorithms** {#3.2-core-algorithms}

* **Listing Search and Filtering:** Retrieves available new and second-hand listings using keywords, category, price range, condition, and location. Sorting and pagination organize the results.  
* **Listing and Favorites Management:** Verifies ownership before editing or removing listings and checks active transaction restrictions. A unique user–listing constraint prevents duplicate favorites.  
* **Offer Negotiation:** Validates listing availability, proposed prices, and participant permissions. Sellers can accept or reject offers, while revised offers remain traceable. Users cannot submit offers on their own listings.  
* **Listing Exchange:** Verifies that selected listings belong to different users, remain available, and support exchange. Acceptance reserves the related listings and creates a transaction through a consistent database update.  
* **Transaction Management:** Creates transaction records from accepted offers or exchange requests. Conditional updates and database transactions prevent conflicting acceptances. Accepted transactions remain separate from completed transactions.  
* **Listing Recommendations:** A basic ranking approach can use recently viewed or favorited categories to suggest available listings. Similar listings can be selected by category and price range, with recent listings used when interaction history is unavailable.  
* **Real-Time Messaging:** Stores messages in PostgreSQL before acknowledging submission and delivers them through Socket.IO. Message identifiers prevent duplicates, while reconnection synchronization retrieves missed messages. Connection tracking supports online/offline status.  
* **Notification Handling:** Stores notification records and sends relevant updates through Socket.IO and FCM. Read status supports notification history and unread counts.  
* **Report Processing:** Records reports for administrator review, tracks their status, and notifies the reporting user of the outcome.  
* **AI Chatbot Assistance:** Provides an LLM with relevant application guidance and permitted listing information. Backend-validated tool calls support listing searches and availability checks. Unresolved questions are directed to support.

## **3.3 Security, Performance, and Reliability Measures** {#3.3-security,-performance,-and-reliability-measures}

* **Authentication and Session Security:** Passwords will be securely hashed. JWT access tokens, refresh-token expiration and revocation, and secure mobile storage will protect user sessions. Email OTPs will expire after five minutes, have limited attempts, and become invalid after use.  
* **Authorization:** Backend permission checks will protect administrator functions, listing ownership, and conversation membership. These checks will apply to both REST APIs and Socket.IO events.  
* **Request Protection:** Input validation and rate limiting will reduce invalid requests, brute-force attempts, and excessive use of sensitive endpoints.  
* **Secure Communication:** HTTPS will protect communication with the backend. Database credentials and external-service secrets will remain on the server and be excluded from application logs.  
* **Database Performance:** PostgreSQL indexes and pagination will support efficient listing searches and message retrieval. Constraints and database transactions will maintain consistent offer, exchange, and transaction records.  
* **Media Validation:** Uploaded files will be checked for permitted types and sizes before storage on Cloudinary. Media operations will require appropriate user permissions.  
* **Messaging Reliability:** Persistent storage, acknowledgments, duplicate prevention, and reconnection synchronization will support reliable messaging. Push delivery will supplement notification records stored in the database.  
* **AI Security:** Chatbot tool calls will use validated arguments and enforce the requesting user’s permissions. Responses will be identified as automated assistance, and unnecessary private information will be excluded from LLM requests.  
* **Monitoring and Recovery:** API documentation, health checks, and application logs will support maintenance. Configured Amazon RDS backups and tested restoration procedures will support database recovery.

# **Chapter 4: Functional Requirements** {#chapter-4:-functional-requirements}

## **4.1 Functional Requirements** {#4.1-functional-requirements}

### **4.1.1 User** {#4.1.1-user}

* **Authentication:**  
  * The system allows unregistered users to create a new account by providing a username, email, and password or using Google registration.  
  * The system allows registered users to log in to access shopping features.  
  * The system supports a "Forgot Password" function via an OTP sent to email, which is valid for 5 minutes.  
  * The system supports registration email OTP verification and Google OAuth login to reduce account creation friction while preserving account security.  
  * Users can securely log out of the system.  
* **Profile Management:**  
  * Users can view and update personal information, including full name, gender, date of birth, phone number, and avatar.  
  * The system allows users to manage their delivery addresses and change their login password.  
* **Listing Discovery:**  
  * The system displays available listings with images, names, prices, conditions, and locations.  
  * Guests and registered users can view listing details, including descriptions, images, categories, conditions, prices, availability, and seller information.  
  * The system provides a search function that allows users to find listings by name or keywords.  
  * Users can filter listings by category, price range, condition, and location.  
  * Users can browse discovery sections such as personalized recommendations, featured listings, best sellers, trending listings, similar listings, and recently viewed listings.  
  * Users can sort listings by price or posting date.   
* **Listing Listing Management:**  
  * Registered users can post second-hand or new listings by providing a listing name, description, category, condition, price, location, and images.  
  * Users can specify whether a listing is available for sale, exchange, or both.  
  * Users can view and edit their own listing listings.  
  *  Users can remove their listings when they are no longer needed, subject to any active transaction restrictions.  
  * Users can update listing statuses to available, reserved, sold, or exchanged.  
* **Favorite Management:**

  * The system allows registered users to start a conversation with a seller from a listing listing.  
  * Buyers and sellers can send and receive messages in real time.  
  * Users can discuss listing conditions, prices, meeting locations, and trading arrangements.  
  * User can view previous conservations and message history  
  * The system restricts conversation access to the participating users.  
* **Buyer-Seller Messaging:**  
  * Buyers can send a price offer for an available listing.  
  * Sellers can view incoming offers and accept or reject them.  
  * Buyers and sellers can negotiate and submit revised offers.  
  * Users can view the proposed price, related listing, participants, and current status of each offer.  
  * The system prevents users from submitting offers on their own listings or on unavailable listings.  
* **Listing Exchange**

  * Users can propose an exchange by selecting one of their available listings and another user’s listing that supports exchanges.  
  * The receiving user can view the proposed listing and accept or reject the exchange request.  
  * Users can discuss exchange arrangements through messaging.  
  * Users can view the status of their sent and received exchange requests.  
  * The system prevents exchange requests involving the same owner or unavailable listings.  
* **Reports:**

  * Users can report inappropriate listing listings or user behavior by selecting a reason and providing a description.

  * The system records reports and makes them available for administrator review.

  * Users can view the status and outcome of their submitted reports.  
* **Notifications:**

  * Users receive real-time notifications about new messages, offers, exchange requests, and transaction updates.

  * The system notifies users when their offers or exchange requests are accepted or rejected.

  * Users receive notifications about moderation actions affecting their listings or accounts and the outcomes of their reports.

  * Users can view notification history and mark notifications as read.  
* **Offers and Negotiation:**  
  * Buyers can send a price offer for an available listing.  
  * Sellers can view incoming offers and accept or reject them.  
  * Buyers and sellers can negotiate and submit revised offers.  
  * Users can view the proposed price, related listing, participants, and current status of each offer.  
  * The system prevents users from submitting offers on their own listings or on unavailable listings.  
* **Boosted Listings**   
  * Registered sellers can boost their own active listings.  
  * The system displays available boost packages with duration and price.  
  * The boost is activated after successful payment.  
  * Sellers can view the boost status and expiration time.  
  * Draft, pending, hidden, rejected, or sold listings cannot be boosted.  
* **Chatbot Support:**  
* The system provides a chatbot that allows guests and registered users to ask questions about the application.  
* The chatbot provides guidance on account registration, listing posting, searching, favorites, messaging, offers, and listing exchanges.  
* The chatbot answers frequently asked questions about transaction procedures and platform rules.  
* When the chatbot cannot resolve a question, it guides users to contact support or submit a report.  
* The system clearly identifies chatbot responses as automated assistance.

### **4.1.2. Admin** {#4.1.2.-admin}

The original draft modeled Admin as a retail store operator (creating listings, managing stock/variants, processing orders, issuing discount coupons). In a C2C marketplace, users own their own content and transactions; Admin's job is platform integrity and moderation, not inventory or order management. The functions below replace that section entirely.

* **Listing Moderation:**

  * Admin can view a queue of listings pending review (if pre-publish moderation is enabled) or flagged listings (if moderation is complaint-driven), with filters by category/status/date.

  * Admin can approve, reject (with a required reason), or remove an already-active listing for policy violation; the reason is stored and surfaced to the owner via notification.

  * Admin cannot edit the content of a user's listing (title/price/description) — only approve/reject/remove it. (This is the key correction from the original draft, where Admin could directly "edit existing information" of listings — not appropriate when the listing belongs to a user, not the platform.)  
* **User Management:**

  * Admin can view the list of all users with their profile info, role, verification status, and trust rating.  
  * Admin can issue a warning, temporarily suspend, or permanently ban a user account for policy violations, with a mandatory reason logged.  
  * Admin can view a user's report history (both as reporter and as reported party) to support a moderation decision.  
*  **Report Handling:**  
  * Admin can view all submitted reports, filter by status/reason/date, and open each for detail (reporter, target, evidence).  
  * Admin can resolve a report by taking an action (warn/suspend/ban user, remove/keep listing, dismiss) and adding a resolution note.  
  * The system notifies both the reporter (outcome) and, where applicable, the reported party (action taken and reason).  
* **Category & Attribute Management:**  
  * Admin can create, edit, deactivate categories and condition labels (e.g., New, Like New, Used – Good, Used – Fair, For Parts) used when posting a listing.  
  * (No "variant" or "stock quantity" management — secondhand listings are unique units, not manufactured SKUs; see NFR note below.)  
* **Boosted Listings:**  
  * Admin can create, edit, activate, or deactivate boost packages.  
  * Admin can view active, expired, and failed boosts.  
  * Admin can view boost transactions and payment statuses.  
  * Admin can monitor total boost purchases and boost revenue.

●  **Statistics & Reporting (Dashboard)**:

* Admin dashboard shows platform-level KPIs: total active listings, new users (period), completed transactions (period), open reports, and (if boosts are implemented) boost revenue.  
* Admin can view trend charts (new listings, new users, completed transactions) over a selected date range.  
* (Removed: "total orders", "order status distribution" — there is no platform-managed order pipeline in this model; transaction status distribution, as defined in 4.1.8, is the correct equivalent if the team wants a similar chart.)

● **Blog / Content Management** 

* Admin can create, edit, and publish informational posts, including safe-trading tips, buying and selling guides, listing exchange guidance, and platform announcements.  
* Admin can manage each post’s title, content, cover image, and category.  
* Admin can save posts as drafts, temporarily hide published posts, or archive outdated content.  
* Guests and registered users can browse published posts and view their details.  
* Blog content remains separate from listing listings and does not affect offer, exchange, or transaction workflows.

● **Chatbox / Support Management:**

* If the chatbot is implemented, Admin can view conversations the chatbot could not resolve and reply directly, with conversation history visible for context.  
* AI Knowledge Management Admins can monitor AI catalog synchronization status, manually trigger catalog indexing, upload/delete RAG documents, and keep listing/promotion knowledge available for the AI assistant.

## **4.2. Non-functional Requirements** {#4.2.-non-functional-requirements}

Non-functional requirements define the quality criteria for system operation, including security, performance, maintainability, and usability.

* **Security:**  
  * **Authentication and Authorization:** Protected APIs and Socket.IO events must validate JWT access tokens and enforce user permissions. Administrative functions must be restricted to authorized administrators.  
  * **Password and Session Protection:** Passwords must be hashed using bcrypt. Authentication tokens must be stored securely on mobile devices, with expiration and refresh-token revocation supported.  
  * **Data Privacy:** Users must only access conversations, offers, and transaction records they participate in. Listing changes must enforce ownership checks, while blog management must be restricted to administrators.  
  * **API and Upload Protection:** The backend must validate inputs, limit requests to sensitive endpoints, and validate uploaded file types and sizes. Email OTPs must expire after five minutes and have limited verification attempts.  
  * **Secure Communication:** Communication must use HTTPS. Database credentials and external-service secrets must remain on the backend and must not appear in application logs.  
  * **AI Access Control:** Chatbot requests must have usage limits. Any AI tool calls must enforce user permissions and avoid exposing private data.  
* **Performance:**  
  **Mobile Responsiveness:** The Flutter interface must remain responsive during network requests and show loading indicators for ongoing operations.  
  **Data Retrieval:** Listing searches and message history must use pagination. PostgreSQL indexes must support frequently used queries.  
  **Media Optimization:** Images delivered through Cloudinary should be appropriately sized and compressed to reduce loading time and mobile data usage.  
  **Real-Time Communication:** Socket.IO must provide timely messaging and status updates under normal network conditions. Performance testing must record response times under defined network and user-load conditions.  
* **Maintainability & Scalability:**  
  **Architecture:** The system must separate presentation, business logic, and data access. Flutter features must follow Presentation, Domain, and Data layers.  
  **Code Organization:** Feature-based modules and shared components must reduce duplication. API documentation and Prisma migrations must support maintenance.  
  **Deployment:** Backend configuration and secrets must be managed separately from source code. AWS resources must support capacity increases, with shared Socket.IO coordination configured before introducing multiple backend instances.  
* **Usability:**  
  **Adaptive Interface:** Flutter screens must accommodate supported device sizes, readable text, and accessible touch targets.  
  **Clear Feedback:** Validation errors, success messages, and connection states must be easy to understand. Destructive actions must require confirmation.  
  **Marketplace Status:** Listing availability, offer and exchange statuses, and message delivery states must be clearly displayed.  
  **Content Management:** Listing forms and administrator blog editors must provide image previews, validation feedback, and clear publishing or moderation status.  
* **Content Management Usability:**   
  Blog and listing rich-text editors must support readable content creation with image upload, validation feedback, and clear approval status indicators.  
* **Recommendation Transparency:** 

**Recommendations:** Users without sufficient interaction history must receive general discovery results rather than results labeled as personalized.  
**AI Assistance:** Chatbot responses must be identified as automated. When relevant information is unavailable, the chatbot must indicate this and provide an appropriate support option.

The Actor enters the OTP code, password and re-enter the password then press the "Đặt lại mật khẩu" button. The system verifies and then the system updates the new password and redirects the Actor to the homepage. |

If the Actor enters the verification code after 5 minutes, the system will ask the Actor to click the “Gửi lại mã OTP” button. 5.2. If the passwords do not match or contain fewer than eight characters, the system asks the Actor to correct them.  |

### **5.2.11 Negotiate Listing Price**  {#5.2.11-negotiate-listing-price}

##### *Table 5.2.11: Negotiate Listing Price* {#table-5.2.11:-negotiate-listing-price}

| Name | Negotiate Listing Price |
| :---- | :---- |
| **The Actor** | Registered Customer (Buyer), Registered Customer (Seller)  |
| **Trigger** | The Buyer selects the “Trả giá” button.  |
| **Description** | Allows the Buyer and Seller to negotiate and agree on a listing price. . |
| **Pre-Conditions** | The listing is available and allows negotiation.  |
| **Post-Conditions** | The offer result and agreed price are stored in the conversation.  |
| **Main Flow** | The Buyer enters an offer price and sends it to the Seller. The system displays the offer in the conversation. The Seller accepts, rejects, or proposes another price. The system notifies both Actors of the result. If accepted, the system displays the agreed price. |
| **Alternate Flow** | 3.1 The Buyer or Seller may propose another price.  |
| **Exception Flow** | 1.1 If the offer is invalid, the system asks the Buyer to enter another price. 2.1 If the listing is unavailable, the offer cannot be sent.  |

| :---- | :---- |

| **Trigger** | The Actor selects the “Đăng tin” button.  |
| **Description** | Allows the Actor to create a new listing listing.  |
| **Pre-Conditions** | The Actor has logged in.  |
| **Post-Conditions** | The listing is submitted and saved with the appropriate status.  |
| **Main Flow** | The Actor uploads images and enters the listing name, category, and condition. The Actor enters the price, description, location, and contact method. The Actor previews the listing and selects “Đăng tin.” The system saves the listing and sends it for review. |
| **Alternate Flow** | 3.1 The Actor selects “Chỉnh sửa” to modify the information before posting  |
| **Exception Flow** | 3.2 If required information is missing, the system asks the Actor to complete it. 4.1 If an image cannot be uploaded, the system displays an error message.  |

### **5.2.13 Manage Listings**  {#5.2.13-manage-listings}

| :---- | :---- |
| **The Actor** | Registered Customer  |
| **Trigger** | The Actor selects the “Quản lý tin” tab.  |
| **Description** | Allows the Actor to view and manage their listings by status. |
| **Pre-Conditions** | The Actor is logged into the system. |
| **Post-Conditions** | The Actor’s listings are displayed and organized by status.  |
| **Main Flow** | The Actor selects the “Quản lý tin” tab. The system displays the Actor’s listings. The Actor selects a status: Displaying, Pending, Hidden, or Sold. The system displays listings with the selected status. |
| **Alternate Flow** | 3.1 The Actor edits the listing information. 3.2 The Actor hides or restores the listing. 3.3 The Actor marks the listing as sold. 3.4 The Actor deletes the listing. |
| **Exception Flow** | 4.1 If the update fails, the system displays an error message. 4.2 If there are no listings, the system displays an empty-state message.  |

| **Exception Flow** | 5.1 If required information is missing or invalid, the system asks the Actor to correct it.  |

| **Post-Conditions** | The listing status is updated. |
| **Main Flow** | The Actor selects “Ẩn tin.” The system changes the listing status to Hidden. The listing is removed from public search results. |
| **Alternate Flow** | 1.1 The Actor selects “Hiện lại,” and the system makes the listing visible again.  |
| **Exception Flow** | 2.1 If the status cannot be updated, the system displays an error message.  |

### **5.2.16 Mark Listing as Sold**  {#5.2.16-mark-listing-as-sold}

| :---- | :---- |
| **The Actor** | Registered Customer (Seller)  |
| **Trigger** | The Actor selects “Đánh dấu đã bán” on their active listing.  |
| **Description** | Allows the Actor to mark their listing as sold after completing a sale outside the platform.  |
| **Pre-Conditions** | The Actor has logged in, owns the listing, and the listing is currently active.  |
| **Post-Conditions** | The listing status is changed to Sold and removed from public search results.  |
| **Main Flow** | The Actor opens “Quản lý tin.” The Actor selects “Đánh dấu đã bán” on an active listing. The system displays a confirmation message. The Actor confirms the action. The system changes the listing status to Sold and moves it to the “Đã bán” tab. |
| **Alternate Flow** | 4.1 The Actor selects “Hủy,” and the listing remains active.  |
| **Exception Flow** | 5.1 If the listing status cannot be updated, the system displays an error message.  |

### **5.2.17 Manage User** {#5.2.17-manage-user}

##### *Table 5.2.17: Manage User* {#table-5.2.17:-manage-user}

| Name | Manage User |
| :---- | :---- |
| **The Actor** | Admin |
| **Trigger** | The Actor selects “Người dùng” from the sidebar. |
| **Description** | This use case enables the Actor to manage all the users’ accounts. |
| **Pre-Conditions** | The Actor has already logged into the system. |
| **Post-Conditions** | The Actor can read the analytical dashboards. |
| **Main Flow** | The Actor selects “Người dùng” from the sidebar. The system displays the list of all users’ accounts (excluding the currently logged-in admin), including key information (username, email, fullname, role, creation date) and management buttons (update, delete). The Actor can search for users by keywords (name, email), can filter the users’ list by role, or other available criteria and selects a specific user’s update button to view user details. The system displays the user’s detailed information. The Actor can choose one of the management actions: **5.1 Update User Account** 5.1.1 The Actor selects the “Chỉnh sửa” icon on a specific user.5.1.2 The system displays the editable form with the user’s information.5.1.3 The Actor modifies the desired fields and submits the form.5.1.4 The system validates the input and updates the user’s data.5.1.5 The system displays a confirmation message that the update was successful. **5.2 Delete User Account** 5.2.1 The Actor selects the “Xóa” icon on a specific user.5.2.2 The system displays a confirmation dialog.5.2.3 The Actor confirms the deletion.5.2.4 The system deletes the selected user account.5.2.5 The system displays a confirmation message that the deletion was successful. The system redirects the Actor to the user list or continues managing users. |
| **Alternate Flow** | None. |
| **Exception Flow** | 5.1.4.1. If the Actor adjusts the username into blank, the system will ask the Actor to fill that criteria. |

### **5.2.18 Boost Listing**  {#5.2.18-boost-listing}

##### *Table 5.2.18: Boost Listing*  {#table-5.2.18:-boost-listing}

| Name | Boost Listing  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **The Actor** | Registered Customer (Seller)  |
| **Trigger** | The Actor selects the “Đẩy tin” button on their listing.  |
| **Description** | Allows the Actor to pay a service fee to promote their listing for a selected period.  |
| **Pre-Conditions** | The Actor has logged in, owns the listing, and the listing is currently displayed.  |
| **Post-Conditions** | The payment is completed, and the listing is promoted for the selected period.  |
| **Main Flow** | The Actor selects “Đẩy tin” on an eligible listing. The system displays the available boost packages. The Actor selects a package and reviews the service summary. The Actor selects a payment method and confirms the payment. The system activates the boost and displays its start and end time. |
| **Alternate Flow** | 2.1 The Actor selects another boost package. 5.1 The Actor views the current boost status. 5.2 After the boost expires, the Actor may select “Đẩy tin lại.”  |
| **Exception Flow** | 1.1 If the listing is a draft, pending review, requires revision, rejected, hidden, or sold, the system disables the boost function. 4.1 If the payment fails or is cancelled, the listing is not boosted. 4.2 If the payment is still being verified, the system displays “Đang xác nhận phí dịch vụ” and prevents duplicate payment.  |

##### *Table 5.2.19: AI Assistant*  {#table-5.2.19:-ai-assistant}

| Name | Chatbox |
| :---- | :---- |
| **The Actor** | Registered Customer, Admin |
| **Trigger** | The Actor selects the ReStore AI entry or enters a request in the AI Assistant.  |
| **Description** | Allows the Actor to find, filter, and compare listings using natural-language requests.  |
| **Pre-Conditions** | The AI service is available, and the system has listing data.  |
| **Post-Conditions** | The AI response and relevant listing recommendations are displayed.  |
| **Main Flow** | The Actor opens ReStore AI. The Actor enters a listing-related request. The system analyzes the request and searches for suitable listings. The system displays a response and relevant listing recommendations. The Actor may select a recommended listing to view its details. |
| **Alternate Flow** | 2.1 The Actor selects a suggested question. 4.1 The Actor provides additional requirements to refine the results. 4.2 The Actor asks the AI Assistant to compare recommended listings.  |
| **Exception Flow** | 3.1 If no suitable listings are found, the system displays suggestions for adjusting the request. 3.2 If the AI service fails, display: “Không thể tải kết quả lúc này” and allow the Actor to try again.  |

| **Post-Conditions** | The seller profile is displayed.  |

### **5.2.29 Payment via VNPAY** {#5.2.29-payment-via-vnpay}

##### *Table 5.2.29: Boost Listing via VNPay*  {#table-5.2.29:-boost-listing-via-vnpay}

| Name | Payment via VNPAY |
| :---- | :---- |
| **The Actor** | Registered Customer (Seller)  |
| **Trigger** | The Actor selects “Đẩy tin” for their listing.  |
| **Description** | Allows the Actor to purchase a boost package and pay through VNPay.  |
| **Pre-Conditions** | The Actor is logged in and owns an approved, active listing.  |
| **Post-Conditions** | The payment is recorded and the boost is activated after successful payment.  |
| **Main Flow** | 1\. The Actor selects “Đẩy tin”. 2\. The system displays available boost packages. 3\. The Actor selects a package and confirms the payment. 4\. The system redirects the Actor to VNPay. 5\. The Actor completes the payment. 6\. The system verifies the payment, activates the boost, and displays the successful result. |
| **Alternate Flow** | 5.1. If the Actor cancels the payment, the system displays the cancelled status and does not activate the boost.  |
| **Exception Flow** | 1.1. If the listing is pending, hidden, sold, or inactive, the system disables the boost function. 6.1. If payment fails, the system allows the Actor to try again. 6.2. If payment is pending, the listing remains unchanged until payment is confirmed.  |
